profile.name: Lorenzo Pallanan
profile.title: Self-Taught. Field-Tested.
profile.shortInfo: Driven by the pursuit of building my own development studio, I don't just write code—I build robust technology to solve real-world problems. Whether I am reviving cyber cafes with custom diskless servers, reverse-engineering game servers, or coding private billing portals for Fiber ISPs, I engineer solutions with limitless possibilities.

stats.Philosophy: The Foreman Approach: Architecture over Syntax

profile.fullStory:
I am a self-driven IT Specialist and Systems Developer. My journey didn't follow a traditional academic route—I thrive on relentless curiosity and hands-on discovery. Overcoming early struggles with social anxiety, I found my voice in technology. 

My expertise is built on real-world survival: engineering 10km point-to-point network bridges for family internet cafes, reverse-engineering game servers, and mastering C# and Python for enterprise automation. I operate under what I call the 'Foreman Philosophy': Give a novice a power tool, and they will struggle. Give a master foreman manual tools, and they will build a house. As a developer, I leverage advanced tools like AI not to write for me, but to execute my architectural blueprints with maximum velocity.

Recently, my work has expanded directly into live event production and enterprise ISP management. From operating LED walls for major concerts and weddings to architecting private billing and GIS network mapping systems for a Fiber FTTH ISP, I thrive where physical hardware and complex software intersect.

originStories.title: The Network Architect: PISONETs & 10km Bridges
originStories.story:
My technical foundation was built in the trenches. When my family opened a 'PISONET' (a local internet cafe model), I took over the infrastructure. Bandwidth was scarce, so I engineered a solution using UBNT air networks—pulling a 200mbps connection from a heavy-traffic zone and beaming it 10 kilometers directly to our shops. 

While other shop owners relied on traditional setups, I experimented, studied, and successfully deployed high-performance diskless servers for our entire fleet, proving early on that I could architect enterprise-grade solutions with limited resources.

originStories.title: The Tech Artist: Forging a Game Dev Dream
originStories.story:
In 2020, family illness and the pandemic forced a massive pivot. During this time, a mentor named 'hyblitz' introduced me to game development. I dove in completely self-taught. While I didn't have the artistic skills to draw characters, my grasp of backend systems and logic was immediate. Blitz dubbed me a 'Tech Artist'. 

This led to my first major software deployment: Daddyran Online. By reverse-engineering source code from Ragezone, I successfully launched a fully operational private server and its accompanying web portal. Though it ultimately taught me a harsh lesson in marketing, the technical victory cemented my dream of opening my own development studio.

originStories.title: The Foreman: Mastering Full-Stack & Automation
originStories.story:
Determined to monetize my skills, I began selling web architecture. My first client, Mondragon House, pushed me to master RESTful APIs, databases, and ASP.NET. I quickly became an expert in C#, and recently expanded into Python to build automated web scrapers. 

I am a great developer because I understand the foundation of how things are built. I use AI to accelerate my workflow, but the core architecture, logic, and structure come entirely from my expertise. I am the foreman wielding the power tools to build scalable, high-performance tech.

originStories.title: The Live Stage & The Fiber
originStories.story:
Following my time at Teleperformance in late 2024, I transitioned into a dual role that perfectly blended hardware and software. I became an LED Wall Operator for my cousin's sound system business, staging massive events, pageants, concerts, and weddings. My technical research drastically improved our live production workflows, and being on the ground allowed me to network directly with industry professionals—which is exactly how I landed the contract to build a website for Migs Styling.

Concurrently, I stepped in as a Technician for RPS Networks, a Fiber FTTH ISP. Beyond standard tech duties, I architected a completely private, full-scale billing and network mapping system for them. Managing live visual outputs on stage one day and coding enterprise-level GIS client tools the next is exactly the kind of hybrid systems engineering I live for.

vision.title: My Vision
vision.content: I've always dreamed of starting my own development studio—a place where creativity and technology collide to make awesome web apps, software, and games. I want to lead a team that's just as passionate about innovation as I am.
points: Starting Something New: Building a studio from the ground up.
Creating Cool Tech: Turning new concepts into reality through advanced coding.
Always Learning: Tech is always evolving, and I am relentlessly adapting.
Teamwork: Collaborating with others who share my passion for perfect architecture.

projects.title: ARKA-designs.com
projects.overview: A minimalistic, aesthetic portfolio architecture for a leading designer.

fullStory.content: The client for this project is an architectural designer and a close childhood friend from my local church. He approached me with a straightforward request: build a digital space that reflects his design philosophy.

His core keywords were 'aesthetic' and 'simple'. The primary objective of the platform was to act as a digital portfolio to showcase his high-fidelity physical projects, while simultaneously driving client acquisition through a highly accessible contact pipeline.

To ensure maximum uptime with zero server maintenance costs, the entire application was compiled as a static build, hosted directly through GitHub Pages, and seamlessly linked via custom DNS forwarding to his primary domain.

Finally, foundational SEO mechanics—including metadata optimization and semantic structure—were integrated into the build. This ensures the portfolio is easily discoverable by search engines, helping drive organic traffic and turning local architectural queries into actual client leads.

projects.title: MigsStyling.com
projects.overview: A pixel-perfect brand platform for an elite luxury event styling and coordination team.

fullStory.content: I crossed paths with the incredible Host Jay Ramos while operating LED walls and visual production for Soundmax Lights and Sounds at a live event. Recognizing the elite caliber of their work, I took the initiative to reach out directly. The timing was absolute perfection—they were just about to sign another developer to build their digital platform.

Migs Styling, owned by Sir Migs and Host Jay, is a top-tier production styling team renowned for their luxurious designs. They possess the unparalleled ability to transform even the most basic space—literally turning a garage into a breathtaking, high-end venue.

Host Jay spearheaded the digital project with a strict, highly detailed vision. As luxury designers, their attention to detail was absolute. Every element—from typography and color palettes to the overarching theme—had to meet their exact standards. I engineered a clean, elegant web architecture that perfectly mirrored their physical styling capabilities, and they loved the final result.

The success of this build has evolved into an ongoing partnership. We are currently architecting a comprehensive, automated wedding ecosystem designed to provide couples with their own personalized websites, digital invitations, and seamless online guest reservations.

projects.title: RPS Network Billing & Mapping System
projects.overview: Private enterprise management tool for a Fiber FTTH ISP.

fullStory.content: I architected this fully private, full-stack internal management system specifically to help my cousin track, monitor, and efficiently scale his growing Fiber ISP client base.

The application features a comprehensive backend routing architecture that drives a custom SQL billing engine. It handles complex data relationships across client profiles and service plans, and safely loops through active subscriptions to auto-generate missing monthly invoices.

Alongside the advanced billing logic, the platform utilizes interactive GIS network mapping. This allows the team to visually track physical fiber lines and client PPPoE nodes directly from the OLT to the NAP.
Due to strict NDA and internal security protocols regarding sensitive customer topography and network data, complete source code and live previews are strictly restricted.

projects.title: Stage & LED Visualizer
projects.overview: Unity 6 URP environment for mapping concert stages to Resolume Arena.

fullStory.content: While operating under Soundmax Lights and Sounds alongside Sir Ryan, a client requested a visual layout for an upcoming live event in Tarlac to better understand the setup. I jumped into Unity 6 URP and engineered this 3D environment to give them a high-fidelity preview of the stage and lighting.

To build the simulation, I developed custom movement scripts for object tracking. To ensure accurate physical-to-virtual stage calibration, boundaries are mathematically calculated relative to the object's initial position rather than fixed world coordinates.

My ultimate vision for this project is to evolve it into a proprietary, standalone application for rapid 3D venue layout. By fully integrating the Unity output with Resolume Arena media server software, it will act as a complete 'virtual training center' and pre-visualization engine for live LED wall mapping.

projects.title: Daddyran Online
projects.overview: Customized private game server, reverse-engineered from source code.

fullStory.content: My first foray into game deployment. I scraped Ragezone for source code and successfully reverse-engineered the backend to launch my own private server. Alongside the server, I built the accompanying web portal, customized the server database with enhanced security, and deployed the full game client.

Despite the technical achievement of getting the game running smoothly, the project met its demise on the business side. I experienced significant difficulties with marketing the server, which eventually led to it going offline due to a lack of an active player base.

However, this experience laid the groundwork for my future ambitions. Instead of relying on scraped code, my ultimate goal is to architect, develop, and launch an entirely original MMORPG from the ground up.

projects.title: Mondragon & TSG Portals
projects.overview: The evolution from IIS-hosted backend portals to the modern TSG React architecture.

fullStory.content: The Mondragon and original TSG portals were my comprehensive web platforms, fully designed and hosted on a dedicated personal IIS server. They were heavily backend-focused, integrating secure social OAuth logins (Google and Facebook), RESTful APIs for feedback databases, and strict input validation.
While Mondragon served as an incredible testing ground for managing server infrastructure and user authentication, the legacy platform is currently offline due to ongoing server transitions.

However, the DNA of those original portals lives on. Taking the lessons learned from managing heavier, server-dependent builds, I completely re-architected my digital presence. This evolution led directly to the development of the new TSG platform you are browsing right now—a blazing-fast, frontend-driven React architecture built for maximum aesthetic impact and flawless uptime.
